title: Packing the Backpack
statement:
You are going on a hike. Your backpack can carry at most **W** kilograms. There are **n** items; item i weighs w[i] kilograms and is worth v[i] points of happiness. Each item can be taken **at most once** (you either take it or you leave it).

What is the maximum total happiness you can carry?
input:
The first line contains two integers **n** and **W**.

Each of the next n lines contains two integers w[i] and v[i].
output: Print one integer: the maximum total value of items whose total weight is at most W.
hints: Trying every subset takes 2^n steps: impossible for n = 100.
Let best[c] be the best value with total weight at most c using the items processed so far. For each item, update c from W down to w[i].
Values add up to 10^11: use 64-bit integers.
editorial:
0/1 knapsack DP. Keep `best[c]` for capacities 0..W, initially 0. For each item (w, v) go through c from W down to w and set `best[c] = max(best[c], best[c - w] + v)`. Going **downwards** guarantees each item is used at most once, because `best[c - w]` still describes the state before this item. The answer is `best[W]`.

Complexity: O(n·W) time, O(W) memory.
